correctness.rationale: From unsigned incidence B, the identities A=BᵀB−2I and BBᵀ=(N−2)I+11ᵀ split the space into constants, centered incidence image, and ker B, the last zero dimensional at N=3. On each bipartite detector component an alternating vertex labeling gives one degree of freedom, including an isolated vertex; an odd cycle kills it. Centering removes one degree iff at least one such component is unbalanced. The bottom-sector vectors zero on D are the zero extensions of ker B_G, giving |E(G)|−N+b(G). The constant sector contributes no dark state for nonempty D. The sum of the two nonnegative dark nullities gives the formula, and the second vanishes exactly when each connected component is a tree or odd-unicyclic. Positivity of the detector rates identifies real-eigenvalue modes with these dark modes through the imaginary part of the eigenvalue equation. The dark span reduces the Hamiltonian, has unitary evolution, and the finite-dimensional complementary generator has strictly negative spectral real parts even if it has Jordan blocks; hence pure- and mixed-state projection formulas. At least M−N detectors are needed to observe ker B. The odd spanning cycle or odd (N−1)-cycle with a leaf leaves a connected nonbipartite detector graph at N≥5: for odd N≥7 the distance-two edges connect the complement and 0,2,4 form a triangle; for even N≥6 the leaf attaches in the complement to every cycle vertex but its old neighbor, which has other complement neighbors, and the leaf and two nonconsecutive nonattachment vertices form a triangle. For N=5 the complement is a five-cycle. The N=3 and N=4 lower bounds are the respective middle multiplicities, two and three; the displayed stars attain them (complements are, respectively, an edge with an isolated vertex and a triangle with an isolated vertex). Thus all placement, threshold, and gap statements are correct in the stated regime. Frozen numerical checks were inspected as corroboration, not executed or used to prove general statements.
